Question: Can one suffocate on a CPAP machine?
Answer: No. If for some reason your mask became completely blocked, your mouth will fall open and you'll be just fine, if you're using a nasal mask. Some people are naturally "mouth breathers" and need to use a CPAP mask that covers the entire nose and mouth in order to maintain airway pressurization. Even in this case, if the machine stopped working, there's still plenty of air that can pass through the unit to keep you alive. Think of a window fan blowing air into a room. Even if the fan is turned off, air is still free to pass through the fan. This is essentially how a CPAP machine works. Now, let's say through some weird circumstances that the hose to your mask became completely clogged, and you were using a full face mask. You'll still be fine. You'll basically have what polysomnographers call a "full arousal". At first, you'll struggle a bit to breathe, just like you do during sleep apnea. Once your blood oxygen levels dip low enough, your subconscious brain will arouse your consciousness to deal with the problem. You'll most likely wake up for just a few seconds to yank the mask off and then go right back to sleep. So quit worrying and use your CPAP like you know you're supposed to. It's not going to kill you, but not using it eventually will. :-)
